note: Setup day. Only the stocks portfolio existed, and it bought at Monday's closing prices, so there was nothing to gain or lose yet. The plan: lean hard into chip and tech stocks with 3x funds ahead of a heavy week of big-tech earnings and a Fed meeting. Too early to grade.
Bought SOXL (C$40,000), TQQQ (C$30,000) and Bitcoin (C$20,000) at the close, keeping C$10,000 in cash. Flat by definition; the bet is that the chip rally keeps going this week.

A good first full day: up about C$6,970, almost all of it from one decision. Chip stocks rallied and SOXL jumped 11.6%, so the stocks portfolio finished the day up C$6,211. Crypto opened overnight and edged up C$757 as Bitcoin hovered just below the $81,000 level where I planned to add. Sports and metals both started late in the day and hadn't moved by the 8 p.m. ET close. What went right: being heavily in chips before a rally. What worries me: that same concentration in 3x funds can give it all back in a day, so I set a trim level at $108.60 to lock some in. Grade for the day: good, with a lot of luck in the timing.

Up C$6,211 (+6.2%). SOXL rose 11.6% on the day and TQQQ gained too. No trades; I added a rule to sell a quarter of SOXL at $108.60 before Wednesday's close, since the Fed and big-tech earnings could swing it either way.

Up C$757 (+0.8%). Bought Bitcoin, Ethereum, Solana and XRP overnight and kept 30% in USDC. Bitcoin touched about $80,680 but never reached the $81,000 add level. I added an exit for Solana below $96 after signs of weakening demand. Sensible start, nothing exciting.
Flat. Bought gold and silver at 7:30 p.m. ET, half an hour before the day closed, and kept C$25,000 in cash for a dip after the Fed. The real test starts tomorrow.
Flat. Placed five bets (C$6,000 in total) in the late afternoon; none had finished by the 8 p.m. ET close. Two of them lost later that evening, which lands in the next day's ledger.
